source.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning

accepted.question_text: For federated learning research across cross-device and cross-silo settings, how can the community define standard evaluation metrics and benchmark datasets that are representative of real-world federated deployments, including non-IID, unbalanced, privacy-sensitive, and scale-sensitive conditions?

evidence.quote: Developing standard evaluation metrics and establishing standard benchmark datasets

accepted.question_text: In fully decentralized or peer-to-peer federated learning, where no central server orchestrates training and clients communicate over a possibly dynamic graph, what governance or trust mechanism should decide the model, algorithm, hyperparameters, and debugging responsibility for a learning task?

evidence.quote: Who decides what is the model to be trained in the decentralized setting?

accepted.question_text: For fully decentralized learning with peer-to-peer client communication, can deep-learning and stochastic-gradient-descent schemes remain robust when clients temporarily disappear, join, drop out, or experience message loss, while still converging in realistic networks?

evidence.quote: for the case of deep learning and SGD this remains an open question

accepted.question_text: For fully decentralized learning under non-IID client data, how can one understand convergence and design model-averaging policies that achieve the fastest convergence, especially when clients perform several local update steps before communication?

evidence.quote: understanding the convergence under non-IID data distributions

accepted.question_text: In fully decentralized federated learning, how can personalized-model methods and incentive or mechanism-design schemes be made robust to malicious actors, unreliable labels, unreliable data, and the absence of a trusted central server?

evidence.quote: robustness of such schemes to malicious actors

accepted.question_text: Can compressed-communication and sparse-update methods developed for centrally orchestrated federated learning be translated to fully decentralized learning without harming convergence, while also enabling better privacy-utility trade-offs than local differential privacy alone?

evidence.quote: without negatively impacting the convergence is an active research direction

accepted.question_text: In cross-silo federated learning, especially when participating organizations may also be competitors, how should incentives be designed to reward honest participation, divide value created by the jointly trained model, optimize participation, and connect incentives with defenses against adversarial data owners?

evidence.quote: incentive mechanism design for honest participation

accepted.question_text: For cross-silo federated learning, what formal privacy guarantees are appropriate when client organizations may control data from many users, may distrust other clients more than the server, and may require local or user-level differential privacy depending on the application?

evidence.quote: This area has not been systematically explored.

accepted.question_text: For split learning, where clients compute early layers and send intermediate activations or gradients rather than raw data, how can split learning be parallelized on edge devices and given formal privacy guarantees for the information revealed by communicated values?

evidence.quote: analysis providing formal privacy guarantees specifically for split learning is still an open problem

accepted.question_text: How should real-world cross-client differences in federated datasets be characterized across feature-distribution skew, label-distribution skew, concept drift, concept shift, quantity skew, violations of independence, and dataset shift so that realistic non-IID benchmarks and mitigation strategies can be built?

evidence.quote: the characterization of cross-client differences

accepted.question_text: Can federated optimization algorithms be designed specifically for federated constraints such as non-IID and unbalanced data, limited communication bandwidth, unreliable availability, client sampling, stateless cross-device clients, and compatibility with privacy and secure aggregation mechanisms?

evidence.quote: target the characteristics of the federated learning setting

accepted.question_text: For federated averaging and local-update stochastic gradient methods, can theory identify when local steps help or hurt convergence, close the gap to accelerated mini-batch SGD in IID settings, and handle asynchronous or straggler-tolerant variants under realistic federated constraints?

evidence.quote: There are many open questions in federated optimization

accepted.question_text: For personalized federated learning, how can model architectures incorporate user and context features, how should multi-task or clustered-client algorithms choose the number and grouping of models, and under what conditions is a shared global federated model better than independent per-client models or personalized local fine-tuning?

evidence.quote: when is a global model better?

accepted.question_text: How can model-agnostic meta-learning and learning-to-learn methods be adapted to federated learning, including realistic benchmarks, theoretical guarantees, personalized-performance metrics, explanations for why globally optimized models may personalize poorly, treatment of concept drift, and possible non-parameter-transfer algorithms?

evidence.quote: with many open questions

accepted.question_text: How can hyperparameter optimization, neural architecture search, debugging, interpretability, and other centralized machine-learning workflow practices be adapted to federated learning when training is slower, resources are limited, hyperparameters include both server and client choices, and raw decentralized data cannot be inspected directly?

evidence.quote: Developing privacy-preserving techniques to answer such questions

accepted.question_text: For federated communication and compression, what are the optimal trade-offs between communication cost and accuracy, how can statistical lower-bound theory guide practical training methods, and can compression be co-designed with secure aggregation and differential privacy rather than treated separately?

evidence.quote: Joint design of compression methods

accepted.question_text: Can federated learning be extended beyond supervised learning to reinforcement learning, semi-supervised learning, unsupervised learning, active learning, online learning, and Bayesian uncertainty-aware models while preserving scalability and computational feasibility?

evidence.quote: all present interesting and open challenges

accepted.question_text: How should federated-learning functions be partitioned among trusted execution environments, ordinary cloud computation, and client devices so that key operations such as secure aggregation or shuffling limit server access to raw contributions without making the trusted computing base too large or impractical?

evidence.quote: how to partition federated learning functions

accepted.question_text: For user-level central differential privacy in cross-device federated learning, how can algorithms adaptively bound heterogeneous user contributions, clip model updates, characterize privacy-accuracy trade-offs when user contribution counts vary widely, and determine whether privacy-amplification-by-iteration results extend to non-convex learning?

evidence.quote: user-level DP is fundamentally less understood

accepted.question_text: How can federated-learning implementations of differential privacy be audited for correctness, including black-box testing methods for systems whose organizations do not open-source their code?

evidence.quote: What techniques can be used for testing FL-implementations for correctness?

accepted.question_text: For private federated learning over streaming, time-series, or dynamically evolving data, how can models be privately updated as new data arrive, how can synthetic data be updated federatedly and privately, and how can private dynamic-database or change-detection techniques be extended to the federated setting?

evidence.quote: Specific open questions include

accepted.question_text: Against an adversarial server, how can one construct efficient and robust secure aggregation that handles semi-honest setup assumptions, per-round aggregate leakage, sparse vectors, client input well-formedness, and client dropouts at large scale?

evidence.quote: how to construct an efficient and robust secure aggregation protocol

accepted.question_text: For distributed differential privacy in federated learning, what are the optimal privacy, accuracy, and communication trade-offs for secure shuffling, secure aggregation, and finite-precision privatization schemes, including lower bounds and matching upper bounds under fixed communication budgets?

evidence.quote: optimal communication, privacy, and accuracy tradeoffs

accepted.question_text: For distributed differential privacy mechanisms that use discrete finite-support noise because Gaussian mechanisms are incompatible with secure shuffling or secure aggregation implementations, how can privacy accounting be tailored to those discrete noise distributions?

evidence.quote: derive privacy accounting techniques

accepted.question_text: Can communication-efficient sub-model federated learning keep each client's sub-model choice private, characterize practical sparsity regimes, develop sparse secure aggregation for those regimes, co-optimize private information retrieval with secure aggregation, and preserve sparse updates under local or distributed differential privacy?

evidence.quote: keeping the client’s sub-model choice private

accepted.question_text: How should federated-learning systems communicate privacy benefits and limitations to ordinary users, model user privacy preferences, decide who sets privacy and security parameters, and incorporate individual choices about desired privacy levels or allowable inferences?

evidence.quote: the following are open questions

accepted.question_text: How can federated learning provide strong protection against an adversarial server, including efficient verifiability through zero-knowledge proofs or trusted execution environments and practical exploit-resistant TEE platforms with trustworthy links between attested binaries and privacy properties?

evidence.quote: Strong protection against an adversarial server

accepted.question_text: In federated learning under poisoning and evasion attacks, how can defenses be evaluated against realistic adversary capabilities, including Byzantine clients, collusion, targeted backdoors, white-box model access, limited participation, and the distinction between data poisoning and model-update poisoning?

evidence.quote: many other characteristics of an adversary’s capabilities

accepted.question_text: Can data-sanitization and network-pruning defenses for data poisoning be used in federated settings without privacy loss, or do federated systems require new defenses that do not rely on direct client data access or representative holdout data?

evidence.quote: whether data sanitization methods and network pruning methods can be used

accepted.question_text: How should adversarial training and robust optimization be adapted to federated learning when samples may be seen only a few times, data are non-IID, perturbation bounds cannot be chosen by inspecting data centrally, and adversarial-example generation may exceed on-device memory or power budgets?

evidence.quote: Adapting adversarial training methods to federated learning

accepted.question_text: How can federated learning become robust to non-malicious failures such as client reporting failures, secure-aggregation dropouts, data-pipeline bugs, and noisy model updates, while still respecting data-access restrictions that prevent direct inspection of raw client data?

evidence.quote: Developing general-purpose debugging methods

accepted.question_text: When secure aggregation is used for privacy in federated learning, how can systems still defend against adversarial attacks, develop efficient range proofs, and determine which nonlinear or Byzantine-robust aggregation methods can be computed efficiently under secure aggregation?

evidence.quote: how to defend against adversarial attacks when secure aggregation is used

accepted.question_text: In federated learning, how can bias in the data-generating process be detected, mitigated, and corrected after training when data come from user interactions, client sampling, device conditions, product-design effects, and privacy constraints that limit direct bias inspection?

evidence.quote: biases in the data-generated process can be identified or mitigated

accepted.question_text: How can fairness be measured and improved in federated learning when sensitive attributes such as race or gender are unavailable, including scalable use of distributionally robust optimization or multicalibration and new theoretical fairness definitions that do not rely on sensitive attributes?

evidence.quote: measuring and correcting unfairness

accepted.question_text: How can federated learning jointly address privacy, fairness, and robustness, including adaptive differentially private mechanisms that preserve minority-group performance, evaluation of the fairness impact of differential privacy without sensitive attributes, and integrated models that are simultaneously robust, private, and fair?

evidence.quote: robust, private, and fair

accepted.question_text: To what extent does increasing stakeholder and data diversity through federated training improve model fairness, and how do required differential privacy mechanisms affect the fairness, performance, and diversity gains of such federated training?

evidence.quote: diversity, fairness, privacy, and performance

accepted.question_text: How do federated client-sampling constraints such as connection quality, device type, location, activity patterns, local dataset size, latency, and dropout affect fairness, and how can those impacts be mitigated through federated objectives, sampling, scheduling, or online-fairness methods?

evidence.quote: sampling constraints affect the fairness

accepted.question_text: How can cross-device federated-learning systems quantify and mitigate system-induced bias caused by availability profiles, device performance, network connectivity, CPU load, local dataset size, timeouts, and other factors that affect whether a device contributes to a round?

evidence.quote: study how bias can be quantified and subsequently mitigated

accepted.question_text: For practical federated-learning systems, how can composite objective functions and automatic tuning algorithms balance model quality, convergence speed, throughput, fairness, privacy, robustness, and server or client resource use when these goals conflict?

evidence.quote: Defining reasonable composite objective functions

accepted.question_text: Can a portable, fast, lightweight, flexible on-device runtime be built for federated learning so that end-user devices can serialize, receive, interpret or execute, and communicate machine-learning training computations without the limitations of large or unstable framework-specific runtimes?

evidence.quote: no solution exists yet that satisfies these requirements

accepted.question_text: For production cross-silo federated learning, how can systems handle coordination across many organizations, including heterogeneous data generation and labeling, incompatible software stacks, jurisdiction-dependent data-use approvals, policy-enforcing infrastructure, vertical feature partitioning, entity alignment, and missing features?

evidence.quote: many different entities are involved

accepted.question_text: How can the federated-learning community develop new datasets that better represent real-world federated problems, including unbalanced and non-IID client partitions, scale-sensitive cross-device scenarios, metadata such as timestamps or geolocation, and feature-partitioned cross-silo datasets?

evidence.quote: Developing new federated learning datasets

trace.notes: Normalized the input as one zbMATH resolver URL with trailing identifier 7389057. Local shard metadata identified the exact work as 'Advances and open problems in federated learning' with DOI 10.1561/2200000083.

Direct local fetch of the zbMATH URL returned a Cloudflare 403 challenge. Exact-work recovery found the matching arXiv full text, 'Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning' (arXiv:1912.04977v3), and the ar5iv HTML rendering was used as the readable primary source because shell downloads of the PDF failed with DNS resolution errors in the sandbox.

Mapped the HTML source: Section 1 defines federated learning and research framing; Section 2 covers decentralized, cross-silo, and split learning variants; Section 3 covers efficiency, optimization, personalization, ML workflows, communication, and model classes; Section 4 covers privacy tools and threat models; Section 5 covers attacks and failures; Section 6 covers fairness; Section 7 covers systems; Appendix A covers software and datasets.
Extracted research-framing candidates on evaluation metrics and benchmark datasets.
Extracted candidates on decentralized learning, cross-silo incentives and privacy, and split learning.
Extracted candidates on non-IID data, federated optimization, personalization, meta-learning, ML workflows, communication and compression, and extensions beyond supervised learning.
Extracted candidates on TEEs, central and distributed differential privacy, auditing, evolving data, adversarial-server protection, secure aggregation, private sub-models, and user perception.
Extracted candidates on poisoning and evasion attacks, defenses, non-malicious failures, debugging, and robustness under secure aggregation.
Extracted candidates on bias, fairness without sensitive attributes, privacy-fairness-robustness interactions, diversity, and sampling constraints.
Extracted candidates on system-induced bias, system parameter tuning, on-device runtimes, cross-silo infrastructure, and representative datasets.

Rewrote extracted open-challenge statements as self-contained questions, inlining the relevant federated-learning setting, threat model, system condition, or evaluation context when supported by the source text.
Merged near-duplicate executive-summary and body occurrences into thematic questions, preserving the strongest source locator for each cluster.
Accepted 42 items. Each accepted item has a self-contained question, explicit unsolved/open-problem evidence locator, no solved label in the source, and meta.is_solved=false.
Saved final JSON to outputs/parse-paper/zbmath_7389057.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
